Hi All, 
    I have one dataset named test.txt:

A,2,2,6.0
A,2,3,7.0
A,2,4,8.0
A,2,5,9.0
B,1,1,0
B,1,2,1.0
B,1,3,2.0
B,2,1,3.0
B,2,2,4.0
B,2,3,5.0

The map function is:
map123<-function(k, values) {
     v<-strsplit(values, ",")
k1<-vector()
v1<-vector()
for(i in 1:length(v)){
k1[i]<-v[[i]][1]
v1[i]<-paste(v[[i]][2],",",v[[i]][3],",",v[[i]][4],sep="")
}
keyval(k1, v1)
}
The reduce function:
reduce123<-function(key,value){
out.val<-vector()
L<-vector()
for(i in 1:length(key)){
L[i]<-key[[i]][1]
out.val[i]<-unlist(strsplit(value[[i]], ","))[3]
}
keyval(L,out.val)

}

The main command line in R is 
from.dfs(mapreduce(input="test.dat", map=map123, reduce=reduce123))

The result is:
$key
[1] "A" "B"

$val
[1] "6.0" "0" 

Why does the result look like:
$key
[1] "A" "A" "A" "A"  "B" "B" "B" "B" "B" "B"

$val
6 7 8 9 0 1 2 3 4 5

What exactly key and value that reduce function received? 
Also, do you have a better way to debug? cause I can't put print() in either map or reduce function. 

Thanks!!

parts:
I am not totally sure I follow the logic of your program, but maybe this factoid will help. The length (or number of rows when applicable) of a the first argument to the reduce function (key) is always one in the rmr sense. So one reduce call will get a key equal to "A" and the other "B", you seem to expect k and value of the same length. The other thing I suspect is that you are reading a csv file without specifying an input format. It shouldn't work at all, but you just hit a lucky combination that reads it anyway as text. I strongly recommend against ignoring the input format.

To get a list of functions for rmr2

help(package="rmr2")

Reading the tutorial is also a common starting point. 


Antonio
